proposals.title: Still listening
proposals.body: I went round the corner before he had finished talking. He followed my tail. I stopped so he could finish. Neither of us has mentioned which end he is addressing.
proposals.reviewReason: The eel's long body bends into the reef with the head hidden; the wrasse faces the exposed rear body. The direction of attention supplies the wrong-end conversation. No prey or cooperative hunting is invented.

media.creator: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE
media.alt: A greyface moray bends into a reef opening while a green and red cheeklined wrasse faces its exposed rear body.

proposals.title: A better angle
proposals.body: The wrasse said he wanted to show me something. Then he stopped broadside in front of my face. I waited. He turned a little in the light. I said yes, very nice, and he turned the other way.
proposals.reviewReason: The richly patterned wrasse occupies most of the foreground, broadside above the small visible greyface head. The fictional sequence makes this a vanity encounter rather than another threat, cleaning or breathing misunderstanding. Source03 repeats this composition and is held.

media.creator: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE
media.alt: A green and red cheeklined wrasse hovers broadside above the visible head of a greyface moray among reef growth.

proposals.title: A place in the shallows
proposals.body: She was asleep when I settled beside her. I was asleep when someone settled beside me. By the time I woke, there was very little water between any of us. I had missed most of the introductions.
proposals.reviewReason: The spring photograph shows numerous manatees clustered closely in clear shallow water. The imagined arrival sequence and sleep translate a real congregation into a social event. No named companion, reproductive role, human contact or aggressive crowding is asserted.

media.creator: Steve Hillebrand / USFWS
media.alt: Numerous Florida manatees cluster in the clear shallow water of Three Sisters Springs, with trees, banks and refuge barriers around them.

holds.decision: Exact image opened. Source explicitly describes sleeping in shallow sunlit water and uses his for the animal. Sex is not independently established. This is also a low head resting portrait, not a distinct interaction. Held without asserting a verified male identification.
